source.title: Landau theory of quenched criticality in linear in-context learning
source.authors: Daesik Kim; Sun-Mi Choi; Hyojae Jeon; Jung H. Han

record.tranche_reason: It derives quenched prediction-error behavior in a linear ICL model and compares it with an annealed calculation, using a theoretical approach rather than a direct model-size sweep.
record.gate_note: The paper's own equations and analysis report test-error behavior as sample complexity varies. Its numerical figures test the order parameter ξ*, not test error; cited results from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: An analytic study of linear in-context learning (linear ICL). It compares annealed (fluctuation-free) and quenched (cavity) test error and links the test-error singularity at the interpolation threshold τc=1 to diverging sample-to-sample fluctuations. This bears on the sample-wise peak (V3) and on whether variance drives the peak (V6). The quenched error formulas themselves are taken from Lu et al. [7]. The paper's own contributions are the annealed control, the result ce = A(ξ*)χ with A(0)>0, and the field-rounding result. Numerics test only the order parameter ξ*, not test error.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that the double-descent singularity at τc=1 in linear ICL is a critical phenomenon of a quenched disordered system. It comes from diverging connected sample-to-sample fluctuations of the learned parameters, which the annealed scheme lacks, and is governed by a diverging Landau susceptibility. The ridge parameter acts as a conjugate field, and the order parameter reflects the density of flat directions. Numerics confirm the predicted order-parameter phase diagram, including a pseudogap regime.
record.recipe_differences: The paper develops an annealed-versus-quenched analytic theory for linear ICL and numerically extracts the Landau order parameter; it does not reproduce the original model-size, epoch, or sample-size sweeps as a direct empirical double-descent study.
record.method_sensitivity: The singularity is analyzed at fixed finite inverse context length γ in the ridgeless, zero-field limit; positive ridge field makes the susceptibility finite. Large-context behavior also depends on task diversity κ and γ.

fits_no_version.finding: In the large-context regime with κ<1, the order parameter ξ* (linked to the flat-direction density) shows a crossover at τ=κ. This becomes a true phase boundary as γ→0, with a nonanalytic critical point at (κ,τ)=(1,1). The numerics (d=30) confirm this pattern for ξ*, not for test error.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In linear ICL, the effective interpolation threshold, judged by the rank of the relaxation matrix, shifts from τ=1 to τ=κ when task diversity is low and context is long.

record.problems: Test-error findings are analytical/asymptotic rather than a numerical test-error sweep. The numerical simulations use d = 30 and σ = 0, and validate the order parameter rather than test error; no uncertainty estimates for the reported numerical order-parameter results are stated in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No test-error rows were omitted. Figures 1, 3, and 4 report theoretical or numerically extracted order-parameter behavior, not test error, so they were not recorded as rows.

untested.parts: All: only the equilibrium t→∞ solution is analysed.
No explicit or numerical test-error curve versus τ. The behaviour away from the critical point and the strict γ→0 limit are not analysed for test error.
All: the study covers only one model class and does not run capacity sweeps.
No effective-complexity measure is used to predict peak location across axes. The τ=κ shift appears only in the order parameter, not in test error.
Label-noise dependence (σ is not varied; σ=0 in numerics), multiple or triple descent, and optimally tuned regularization removing the peak.

missing.what: A scope condition: the divergence of ce via A(0)>0 holds at fixed γ>0 and is stated not to be uniform in the strict limit γ→0. There is also a limit where the quenched errors stay finite (Eq. 4.6).
missing.locator: Section V A after Eq. (5.12); Section IV Eq. (4.6)

record.verdict_notes: I changed the tranche from T2 to T3 because this is an analytic result in a specific new setting (linear ICL). The test-error divergence is largely inherited from Lu et al. [7] (PNAS 2025); researchers should weigh the R3 and R4 support accordingly. The annealed rows (R1, R2) cannot bear on V3 because τ drops out of that scheme.

versions.untested_parts: Model-wise test-error behavior as model size changes, including a peak near the size that fits the training set.
No numerical test-error sweep over sample counts is reported; the result is an asymptotic theoretical analysis of the singularity at the interpolation threshold.
Capacity sweeps past interpolation across model classes and the general U-shaped-to-double-descent curve.
Whether one effective-complexity measure predicts peak location across model size, epochs, and sample count.
The study analyzes positive ridge field versus zero field, but does not test label-noise dependence, multiple or triple descent, or optimally tuned regularization.
Whether counting effective parameters converts second descent into an ordinary U-shaped curve.

rows.subject: linear in-context learning (LICL) model
rows.operation_detail: Calculate annealed in-distribution generalization test error as a function of model parameters.
rows.value: The annealed error does not diverge for any parameter values; it does not depend on τ.
rows.note: Annealed calculation is the paper's comparison scheme; the text says sample complexity disappears from this scheme.
rows.check: The annealed scheme has no τ-dependence, so it cannot show a sample-wise curve; it cannot bear on V3 and should be unlinked from it. It is useful as the fluctuation-free control for V6: with connected fluctuations removed, the error never diverges. The state is recast as observed for V6's variance-driven aspect, meaning no peak once variance is removed.

rows.value: The fluctuation coefficient c_e diverges at τc = 1; the paper identifies the resulting prediction-error singularity with the double-descent divergence.
rows.locator: Section IV, Eqs. (4.3)–(4.4); Section V A, Eqs. (5.8)–(5.11)
rows.note: Analytical/asymptotic result; the paper states that c_e ∼ A(ξ*)χ and that A(0) is finite and nonzero for fixed γ > 0.

The result is asymptotic only, with no numerical test-error curve. It also bears on V6, since the singular part is the connected-fluctuation (variance) term E1^Q.

rows.subject: linear in-context learning (LICL) model
rows.operation_detail: Derive the Landau susceptibility and its contribution to quenched test-error fluctuations at nonzero conjugate field.
rows.measure: Landau susceptibility χ and fluctuation coefficient c_e
rows.baseline: At h = 0, χ diverges as |t|⁻¹ at the critical point.
rows.value: χ = 1/√(t² + 4Iκ(γ)h), which is finite for h > 0; c_e is proportional to χ.
rows.note: This establishes rounding for positive field in the stated theory, not an optimization procedure or an optimal-regularization result.
rows.check: A positive ridge field makes χ, and hence ce, finite (Eq. 5.8), which rounds the divergence. The study does not show the peak disappears or address optimally tuned regularization. It shows suppression of the singularity, not removal of a peak.

relationships.condition: Quenched linear ICL, ridgeless (h=0), fixed finite γ>0, both in-distribution (IDG) and ICL test distributions, asymptotic theory
relationships.reason: The fluctuation coefficient ce=A(0)χ with A(0)>0 diverges at τc=1, so test error rises toward the interpolation threshold as samples increase (R3, R4). The base formulas come from Lu et al. [7].
relationships.display_finding: The fluctuation coefficient ce=A(0)χ diverges at τc=1 with A(0)>0, making test error rise toward interpolation under both test distributions.
